The Battle of Parkutta was fought during the Indo-Pakistani war of 1947–1948 in the Gilgit-Baltistan sector at Parkutta, near Skardu, from 14 April to 17 May 1948. The conflict involved the Gilgit Scouts and the Jammu and Kashmir forces. The Ibex Force of the Gilgit Scouts, led by Major Ehsan, planned an ambush on the relief column for the Skardu garrison.}}
The relief column for Skardu, named Z Brigade was formed comprising of 5th and 7th Jammu and Kashmir infantry and including remnants of Previous Column. Major Ehsan and his men prepared to ambush them at Parkutta to prevent further reinforcement of the garrison. The Brigade troops regrouped on 20 April with and on 10 May most of the troops would enter the area Parkutta, chosen for ambush.
The JAK forces previously who held an important peak lost control by a surprise attack on the same day on 10 May as other attack. This left the JAK troops under intense fire with no cover. Major Kripal would request aid from other troops but the constant pressure mounted made it impossible. On 16 May with the fall of Kargil and heavy losses amounting Major Kripal would retreat with his men to Kharmang. Resulting success for Gilgit scouts and Capture of Parkutta.
Background
on the map of modern-day Gilgit-Baltistan.]]
Geography
The Gilgit scouts had take up their place on the bank of Indus at right in a village named Bagicha. They intended to carry out an ambush at Parkutta. Parkutta is  40 miles away from Skardu located in between Kargil an Skardu. On the right bank there is the village of Kharmang and Marol with Bagicha and Totli on the left bank. At Kharmang near a gorge is rope bridge suspended and the Indus river flow quickly.
Preparations
Gilgit scouts
After the retreat of remaining troops of Indian forces from Battle of Thorgo. Major Ehsan was informed by his troops of the formation of Indian Z Brigade, who were headed for the relief of Skardu garrison.
Major Ehsan sent 100 troops under the command of Lieutenant Muhammad khan to ambush the Indian troops headed to Skardu. Later Captain Nek Alam and Subedar Dost Muhammad also joined with additional troops. Captain Muhammad khan made his headquarter at Hotong-Chan near charkatipari and the troops were stationed at the banks and nearby heights.
Z Brigade
In Another attempt to reinforce Skardu a relief column was to be sent under the name of Z brigade. The brigade was comprised of A and B companies of 7th JAK infantry Battalion and they were merged with the troops of previous relief column and Major Coutts men. They went to Parkutta and waited further troops from 5th JAK infantry.
On March 5 most of the 5th JAK infantry under Major Kripal Singh were airlifted to Srinagar with Some troops of there were held at their previous duties at Pakistan border. The B company proceeded first later joined by troops of D company and a column of A company after facing resistance near Parkutta.
The reinforcements under Major Coutts were given the code name Biscuit Column and Major Kripal was made in charge. Major Coutts was ordered to return to Kargil to establish Headquarters. The Raja of Totli gave 400 porters to support the JAK forces to prove his allegiance.
Battle
Ambush
Colonel Sampuran would progress with his force slowly towards Parkutta, 50 miles in 14 days. They arrived at Simrak on 19 April and 2 Companies were sent ahead to spot troops from Gilgit scouts on 20 April. Some of the troops spotted their presence and became even more cautious. The JAK troops also captured an important point above Panda village which gave an edge over Parkutta.
The nearby hill occupied by Gilgit scouts had to be given up. Subedar Dost Muhammed would travel along the Shyok river and crossed the Chorbat pass for a month. The surprise attack by Gilgit scouts was to be launched on 10 May Early morning and Colonel Kripal left for Parkutta on the same day with his troops.
The Vanguard of the Jammu and Kashmir troops was ambushed at Mirpigund which included 150 men. They ambush took a heavy toll on the JAK force since they were caught by surprise in open with no cover. The troops scattered to take cover to return fire and Colonel Kripal sent his message through his troops to companies at Parkutta to aid them. But the troops at Parkutta were also engaged fully unable to help them. The Parkutta garrison abandoned their position and returned to Mirpigund which took five days.
At Kamango a platoon was sent by Gilgit scouts to ambush the company of Colonel Kripal 5 miles towards Kargil side from Parkutta. Colonel Kripal and his men were seriously injured due to the ambush which took place in a tight gorge and suffered heavy losses. The troops escaped from the valley, unable to fight back. On 16 May Lieutenant Kripal Singh and his men kept on giving resistance but was unable to escape unlike the retreat of Colonel Sampuran Singh on May 12 from Ladakh through Marol. They regrouped with Battalion Headquarters on 16 of May and under Colonel Kripal they retreated to Totli.
Aftermath
The Gilgit scouts took control of much ammunition and weapons in a second surprise attack. On 17 of May Parkutta was captured by Gilgit scouts and Colonel Kripal and his men made their effort to escape towards Kharmang.
Since Ibex force was occupied by the siege of Skardu and facing Relief columns from India, Eskimo force of Gilgit scouts was sent by Colonel Pasha towards Kargil. Major Ehsan sent a platoon towards Nubra to block all land routes for reinforcements, Meanwhile, Major Ehsan led his men in pursuit of the retreating column of Colonel Kripal.
